summary:
FireTrace: MODIS & VIIRS Wildfire Harmonisation
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Submission Summary
Executive Summary

From satellite wildfire records from MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) cannot be compared directly due to differing spatial resolutions, overpass times, and detection sensitivities. FireTrace standardizes NASA FIRMS observations into a 23-column schema, models cross-sensor detection counts and radiative power using Negative Binomial and log-linear regression, and delivers an interactive dashboard with burning activity trends. Unlike single-sensor viewers, FireTrace provides unbroken 2000–2026 timelines across five individual satellite platforms (Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21), transparently distinguishes observed from estimated records, and explicitly flags static snapshot boundaries and pending regional parameterizations.
details:
FireTrace – Project Overview

What does our project do?

FireTrace is a wildfire monitoring and analysis platform that uses satellite data from MODIS and VIIRS to understand how fire activity changes across different regions and over time. It brings important wildfire information together in one dashboard, using maps, charts and visual reports.

How does it work?

FireTrace collects and processes satellite fire data, organises it by location and time, and analyses the patterns. It also compares observations from MODIS and VIIRS to help users understand the differences between the two satellite sensors. The results are displayed through an interactive dashboard.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our project makes large amounts of satellite data easier to understand. It helps users explore fire-prone areas, study historical trends and identify unusual patterns. We hope it can support forest departments, researchers and disaster-management teams in improving wildfire monitoring and preparedness.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • React, TypeScript and Vite for the dashboard.
  • Python for data processing and analysis.
  • MODIS and VIIRS for satellite fire data.
  • CSV, JSON and Parquet for handling datasets.
  • GIS and geospatial tools for location-based analysis.
  • Git and GitHub for collaboration and version control.

What makes our project creative?

Instead of just showing fire locations on a map, FireTrace brings together historical analysis, satellite comparison, data harmonisation and regional insights. One of its main focuses is making data from different satellite sensors easier to compare, even though they have different capabilities.

Factors Considered

While developing the project, we considered data accuracy, differences between satellite sensors, geographical coverage, historical patterns, missing data, reliability of results, ease of use and the technical feasibility of the solution.
